Docs·Find your way around

Select parts

Click, add with Shift, toggle with Ctrl, drag a box, or let the app select by shape, colour or name.

Most tools work on the parts you have selected. A selected part gets an outline in the viewport and its row is highlighted in the parts tree.

In the viewport

Click
Select one part. The tree scrolls to its row.
ShiftClick
Add a part to the selection
CtrlClick
Add a part, or take it out if it was selected
CtrlDrag
Box select: draw a rectangle around parts
CtrlShiftDrag
Box select and add to what is already selected
Esc
Select nothing. A click on empty space does the same.

Click, Box or Brush

The selection-tool button in the left toolbar chooses what a drag does. Press it and let go over a row of its list to pick that tool, or let go on the button and click a row. With Edit mesh on, the same button picks pieces of a mesh instead of whole parts.

Click
The usual way: click a part.
Box
A plain left drag draws a rectangle. A part is picked only when one of its own triangles is under the rectangle, not when its bounding box is.
Brush
A left drag paints: every part under the circle is picked. Hold Shift to add to what is picked; without it, every stroke starts from nothing. Drag with the middle button to change the size of the circle: to the right is bigger, to the left smaller.

In every tool, Alt + drag turns the camera.

In the parts tree

Click
Select one part. Click a group to select every part inside it.
CtrlClick
Add or remove one row
ShiftClick
Select every row between the last one you clicked and this one

Let the app select

The card Selection & actions in the right sidebar has buttons for the common cases:

All
Selects every visible part. CtrlA.
Invert
Selects what was not selected, and the other way round. CtrlI.
Clear
Selects nothing. Esc.
Select similar
Adds every part that has the same shape as the selection. Select one bolt, press it, and all the bolts like it are selected.
Select all instances
Adds every part that shares the exact same geometry as the selection: copies of one part, not just parts that look alike. Stricter than Select similar. It is in the command search, the … menu and the right-click menus.
Select the original
Selects the first part of a shape that has copies, frames it, and shows it in the tree.
Make unique
Gives each selected shared part a mesh of its own, so changing, reducing or deleting detail on it leaves the other copies alone. One undo step.
By colour
Selects every part that shares a colour with the selection.
By name
Asks for a pattern and selects every part whose name matches it. Typing screw selects every part with screw in its name, in capitals or not. The pattern is a regular expression, a compact way to describe text, so some characters such as . and * have a special meaning.
By layer
In the command search (CtrlK), Select by layer lists the CAD layers of the scene with how many parts are on each; click one to select them. A part's layer is also a badge in the Properties card, and a click on the badge does the same. Layers come from a STEP file imported with Keep layers on under What to read; a scene saved here keeps them.

Two tools select for you in a cleverer way: Select hidden parts and the size threshold of Delete small parts.

Find what you selected

  • Press ShiftS to scroll the tree to the selected part and open the groups it is in.
  • Press F to frame the selection in the viewport.
  • The status bar shows how many parts are selected. Click that number to frame them.
  • When none of the selection is in the picture, a faint arrow at the edge of the view points to the side it is on. Click the arrow to frame the selection. See Move the view.
  • Properties shows the triangle count of the selection and its share of the scene.

The right-click menu

Right-click a part, in the viewport or in the tree, for a menu of things to do with the selection: frame it, isolate it, select similar parts, copy, duplicate or delete.

Copy and Paste with several groups selected makes a copy of each group, as a whole folder next to its original, with its own pivot. A group inside another selected group is copied along with it. One Undo takes back one group.

A common mistake: dragging without Ctrl turns the view instead of drawing a selection box. Hold Ctrl first, then drag.
